conventions.slot0: built-in eraser; TextureCount excludes it; tile.raw byte 0 = unpainted
conventions.uv_formula: u = worldX * (1/(16*200)) * UScale  ->  one repeat every 32/UScale metres
conventions.painter_order: higher tile index paints over lower (RAW_GenerateSplat, AreaTerrain.cpp:646-768)

base.rule: ground_share >= 25% with clump >= 5.2, or >= 12% with clump >= 5.2 and solid_frac >= 0.20

mid.definition: secondary ground painted as a stipple/dither over the base; large area, almost no solid interior

cliff.definition: rock skin confined to steep faces
cliff.rule: mean slope >= 28 deg (or >= 60% of tiles above 20 deg) AND slope >= 1.25x the map's own mean slope

path.definition: road, paved trail or plaza -- tiny area, deliberately solid, on flat ground
path.rule: ground_share < 4% AND clump >= 6.0 AND solid_frac >= 0.35 AND mean slope < 15 deg

shore.definition: water margin: beach, riverbed, wet sand
shore.rule: >= 70% of tiles within 4 m of a water cell AND >= 1.6x the map baseline AND slope < 25 deg (skipped for palettes whose maps are themselves mostly waterfront)

void.definition: pure-black fill used as 'no terrain' under block dungeons

unused.definition: palette slot that no corpus map that loads the set ever paints
unused.rule: 0 tiles across every map using the textureset

empty.definition: declared TextureCount covers the slot but no Texture%03d block exists; tile.raw bytes here draw the error texture

role_taxonomy._rejected_role_interior: tested and dropped: dungeon-art textures behave functionally as base/mid/cliff exactly like outdoor ones, so 'interior' is a palette FAMILY (terrainmaps/dungeon/**, zone/dungeon/**), not a usage class. What is genuinely distinct is `void`.
